content: Flavivirus is a genus of viruses belonging to the family Flaviviridae. This genus includes several medically significant viruses such as the West Nile virus, dengue virus, tick-borne encephalitis virus, yellow fever virus, and others that are known to cause encephalitis. These viruses share common structural and genetic characteristics, including a size of 40-60 nanometers, an enveloped icosahedral nucleocapsid symmetry, and a positive-sense, single-stranded RNA genome approximately 10,000-11,000 bases in length. Under an electron microscope, they exhibit a consistent appearance. Replication Flaviviruses possess a positive-sense RNA genome and replicate within the cytoplasm of host cells. Their genome mimics cellular mRNA in most aspects, except for the absence of a polyadenylated (poly-A) tail. This feature allows the virus to hijack the host's cellular machinery to synthesize both structural and non-structural proteins during replication. The host cell's ribosome plays a critical role in translating the viral RNA, similar to how it processes cellular mRNA, resulting in the production of a single polyprotein. Once translated, the polyprotein undergoes cleavage by a combination of viral and host proteases, releasing mature polypeptide products. However, cellular post-translational modifications, which typically depend on the presence of a poly-A tail, are not required for flavivirus replication. Instead, the polyprotein contains an autocatalytic feature that enables the release of the first peptide, a virus-specific enzyme. This enzyme subsequently cleaves the remaining polyprotein into individual functional products. One of the cleaved products is a polymerase enzyme responsible for synthesizing a complementary negative-sense RNA molecule. This negative-sense RNA serves as a template for the production of new genomic progeny RNA. The assembly of new viral particles occurs during the budding process, which also facilitates the acquisition of the viral envelope and leads to cell lysis. Species and Groups The genus Flavivirus includes a wide range of species, categorized based on their mode of transmission and host specificity. These include: Tick-Borne Viruses Mammalian tick-borne viruses: Gadgets Gully virus (GGYV) Kadam virus (KADV) Kyasanur Forest disease virus (KFDV) Langat virus (LGTV) Omsk hemorrhagic fever virus (OHFV) Powassan virus (POWV) Royal Farm virus (RFV) Tick-borne encephalitis virus (TBEV) Louping ill virus (LIV) Seabird tick-borne viruses: Meaban virus (MEAV) Saumarez Reef virus (SREV) Tyuleniy virus (TYUV) Mosquito-Borne Viruses Aroa virus group: Aroa virus (AROAV) Dengue virus group: Dengue virus (DENV) Kedougou virus (KEDV) Japanese encephalitis virus group: Cacipacore virus (CPCV) Koutango virus (KOUV) Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV) Murray Valley encephalitis virus (MVEV) St. Louis encephalitis virus (SLEV) Usutu virus (USUV) West Nile virus (WNV) Yaounde virus (YAOV) Kokobera virus group: Kokobera virus (KOKV) Ntaya virus group: Bagaza virus (BAGV) Ilheus virus (ILHV) Israel turkey meningoencephalomyelitis virus (ITV) Ntaya virus (NTAV) Tembusu virus (TMUV) Spondweni virus group: Zika virus (ZIKV) Yellow fever virus group: Banzi virus (BANV) Bouboui virus (BOUV) Edge Hill virus (EHV) Jugra virus (JUGV) Saboya virus (SABV) Sepik virus (SEPV) Uganda S virus (UGSV) Wesselsbron virus (WESSV) Yellow fever virus (YFV) Viruses with No Known Arthropod Vector Entebbe virus group: Entebbe bat virus (ENTV) Yokose virus (YOKV) Modoc virus group: Apoi virus (APOIV) Cowbone Ridge virus (CRV) Jutiapa virus (JUTV) Modoc virus (MODV) Sal Vieja virus (SVV) San Perlita virus (SPV) Hepatitis C virus (HCV) Rio Bravo virus group: Bukalasa bat virus (BBV) Carey Island virus (CIV) Dakar bat virus (DBV) Montana myotis leukoencephalitis virus (MMLV) Phnom Penh bat virus (PPBV) Rio Bravo virus (RBV) This detailed classification highlights the diversity of flaviviruses and their significant impact on human and animal health.
